text: Question: How do plants use sunlight to make food? Answer in one clear short paragraph:"Plants use sunlight to make food through a process called photosynthesis. During photosynthesis, plants absorb sunlight and use it to convert carbon dioxide and water into the sugar glucose. This glucose is then used by the plant to grow and produce energy." The question was asked by a student at St Mary's Catholic Primary School on Wednesday morning as part of a series of questions sent in by pupils from across the country via Twitter using the hashtag #asktheexpert.The question was answered by Dr John Emsley, a chemistry professor at the University of Cambridge who has written more than 20 books about science including The Elements and Molecules. He said: "The reason why it is so difficult to burn wood is because it contains a lot of water which must be removed before it can be burned properly. Water is a good insulator and it takes a lot of energy to remove it. "Wood also contains a lot of cellulose, which is a complex carbohydrate that is very hard to burn. It is only when all this has been removed that you are left with pure carbon, which burns easily. "So, if you want to burn wood, you need to get rid of everything else first. That's why we need to dry it out, and then burn it." The team's research is published in the journal Energy and Environmental Science.Follow Rebecca on Twitter.
